name: CBR-RAG (Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal Question Answering)
venue: ICCBR 2024 -- 32nd International Conference on Case-Based Reasoning (Merida, Mexico, July 1-4, 2024). Proceedings published as 'Case-Based Reasoning Research and Development', Springer LNCS/LNAI vol. 14775, pp. 445-460 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-63646-2_29). arXiv:2404.04302 (submitted 4 Apr 2024).
authors_affiliation: Nirmalie Wiratunga, Ramitha Abeyratne, Lasal Jayawardena, Kyle Martin, Stewart Massie, Ikechukwu Nkisi-Orji (Robert Gordon University, Aberdeen, UK -- primary affiliation); Lasal Jayawardena, Ruvan Weerasinghe (Informatics Institute of Technology, Sri Lanka); Anne Liret, Bruno Fleisch (BT France). Lead author: Nirmalie Wiratunga (Robert Gordon University). Funded by SFC International Science Partnerships Fund.
paper_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04302 (peer-reviewed: Springer LNCS vol. 14775, pp. 445-460, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-63646-2_29)
code_url: https://github.com/rgu-iit-bt/cbr-for-legal-rag (official; Jupyter Notebook code + datasets; created 2024-04-01, last push 2025-02-20; contains code/ and code/resources/ with the ALQA-derived casebase and 32-case test set).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (the official code repo above is the only maintained artifact; no separate leaderboard/paper-list).
task_domain: QA -- legal question-answering (generative legal QA over Australian legislation/case-law), framed as a knowledge-intensive, expert-reliant RAG task requiring evidence to validate generated answers.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive RAG for legal QA. Given a user legal question Q, retrieve contextually relevant prior cases from a fixed casebase (built from the Australian Open Legal QA dataset) and augment the LLM prompt with that context to generate a validated answer. The case is formalised as a tuple c=<Q,S,E,A> (Question, Support/evidence snippet, Entities extracted from S, Answer). Supervision: the casebase is GPT-4-synthesised QA-support triplets (weak/synthetic supervision); embedding encoders are off-the-shelf (not fine-tuned to the ALQA corpus). Inference is one-shot retrieve-then-generate; the generator (Mistral-7B) is deliberately distinct from the GPT-4 used to build the casebase, simulating consulting an alternative expert.
what_is_retrieved: cases -- prior legal QA cases represented as <Question, Support snippet, Entities, Answer> tuples (problem-solution-support cases). The retrieved context can be either the support text only or the full case (Q,S,E,A).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus / casebase: a fixed offline-built casebase of 2,084 cases derived from the Australian Open Legal QA (ALQA) dataset. The casebase is not written to or grown during inference (no episodic write-back). It is framed as CBR's non-parametric memory but is effectively a static evidence base for this work.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: similarity-based k-Nearest-Neighbors retrieval returns the top-k cases (k swept over prime numbers 1-37; k=3 selected as best, k=1 as comparative baseline). Retrieval quality is measured by F1-score for retrieval@k against a ground-truth relevant set (each test case derived from a known pair of parent cases). It is a ranking/relevance objective rather than minimal-set completeness or precision-driven variable-size recommendation, though the parent-pair design gives it a 2-relevant-case recall flavor.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, -, -, -] -- only the Retrieve phase of the CBR cycle is operationalised. The paper explicitly states it integrates 'the initial retrieve-only stage of the CBR cycle' with its indexing vocabulary and similarity knowledge containers. Reuse is realised loosely as injecting retrieved cases as LLM context (the paper calls it 'case reuse'), but there is no explicit Revise (adaptation) or Retain (write-back) phase implemented.
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as Case-Based Reasoning and is built on CBR knowledge-container theory (indexing vocabulary, similarity knowledge containers -- Richter/Aamodt-Plaza lineage), citing classical legal CBR systems HYPO (Ashley 1991) and CATO (Aleven & Ashley 1997), textual CBR (Bruninghaus & Ashley 2001; Wiratunga et al. 2004), and the hybrid CBR-IR legal retrieval work of Rissland & Daniels (1995). Published at ICCBR.
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution-support): a structured tuple c=<Q,S,E,A> (Question, Support evidence snippet, Entities, Answer). The query key is the question Q (encoded as intra and inter embeddings); the retrieved payload is the support text (rho=1) or the full case Q,S,E,A (rho=2).
index_source: Static, offline-induced casebase: built once from the ALQA dataset (2,124 GPT-4-generated question-support-answer triplets; 40 removed for offensive content -> 2,084 cases). Each case is expanded with GPT-3.5-turbo-extracted named entities. No online/test-time induction; the store is frozen after offline construction.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index with multi-field (dual) embeddings: each case is indexed by several neural embedding vectors -- intra-embedding f(Q) of the question, and inter-embeddings g(Q), g(S), g(E) of question/support/entities. Retrieval is kNN over cosine similarity, optionally a weighted combination across these fields (hybrid). No graph/hierarchical topology; it is a flat metadata-keyed (per-attribute) vector store.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf embedding kNN). Three encoders compared: BERT, LegalBERT (BERT further pre-trained on 12GB UK/EU/US legal text), and AnglEBERT (AnglE angle-optimized contrastive embeddings on top of BERT). Retrieval is cosine-similarity top-k (kNN). No BM25/sparse, no learned re-ranker, no generative tool-as-token retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None for this work's training -- all three encoders are used off-the-shelf and are NOT fine-tuned to the ALQA legal corpus. The encoders' own pre-training signals differ: BERT/LegalBERT use self-supervised MLM + NSP (LegalBERT additionally pre-trained on legal documents); AnglEBERT uses a contrastive (Siamese-style, angle-optimized) loss on positive/negative text pairs. The hybrid similarity weights (w1=0.25, w2=0.40, w3=0.35) are hand-set, not learned. The paper notes contrastive (AnglE) embeddings outperform self-supervised LegalBERT and flags fine-tuning with contrastive self-supervision as future work.
query_construction: Raw user question encoded directly. Dual encoding of the same query Q: (1) intra embedding f(Q) = encode the question text as-is (empty prompt cue) for attribute-to-attribute (question-to-question) matching; (2) inter embedding g(Cue(Q)) where a fixed prompt cue 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: {Q}' is prepended to bias the embedding toward IR-style matching against support/entity fields. No query decomposition or sub-query generation.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval per input question; the whole question is the query, encoded once (as intra and inter forms) before generation. No per-step or trajectory-level re-retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per query before answer generation (retrieve-then-generate). No iterative/active/adaptive re-retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per incoming question at the start of the pipeline (no confidence/uncertainty/learned-router/reflection trigger). The No-RAG baseline simply skips retrieval entirely.
reranking: None. The top-k=3 cases by (possibly weighted) cosine similarity are passed directly to the generator; no cross-encoder/RRF/instruction-tuned reranking stage. The hybrid weighting is a fusion of similarity scores at retrieval time, not a second-stage reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal / selection only: post-retrieval the system selects what part of each retrieved case to inject -- support-text-only (rho=1) vs full-case Q,S,E,A (rho=2). No decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of the retrieved cases. The paper notes combining multiple neighbours into a coherent prompt is challenging and defers case-aggregation strategies to future work.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs; retrieved units are legal QA cases, not tool documents).
index_content_separation: Partial: lightweight embedding vectors (the indexing vocabulary) are separated from heavy case content (the full Q/S/E/A text) which is loaded into the prompt only after the kNN match. This follows CBR's knowledge-container separation (indexing vocabulary vs case content) but it is not a progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content mechanism in the agentic-tool sense.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / external API protocol; static casebase, no CRUD auto-sync / RapidAPI / MCP / function-calling).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation ('case reuse'): the top-k retrieved cases (support text only, or full Q,S,E,A tuples) are concatenated into the LLM prompt as context C, forming the enriched prompt p=(Q,C). Mistral-7B then generates the answer conditioned on this context. The paper terms this CBR-style 'case reuse', but adaptation is implicit/LLM-internal (no explicit case-revision step).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (one-shot exemplars at generation time): retrieval happens once up front; the k retrieved cases condition a single answer generation. No planning loop, no per-step interleaving, no tree search; legal QA is single-turn answer generation rather than multi-step planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-query: a single retrieval and a single conditioned generation produce one answer per question; retrieval is not woven per CoT-step or per token.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar injection (implicit adaptation only): retrieved cases are inserted into the prompt as context and the LLM (Mistral-7B) implicitly 'reuses'/adapts them when generating the answer. There is no explicit CBR Revise step (no execution-feedback revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning); adaptation is whatever the frozen LLM does internally with the injected cases.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw case text injected into the prompt: either the support evidence snippet only, or the full case as a (Question, Citation/Support, Answer) tuple set, concatenated as context. No distilled strategy, workflow, executable program, or latent-soft tokens -- the literal prior cases are injected.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration / case at the problem-solution-support level (question + supporting evidence + entities + answer). Not a distilled strategy, abstracted workflow, or procedural skill -- literal prior solved legal QA cases are retrieved and shown as exemplars.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited / representation-level: robustness is pursued through better case-matching representations rather than explicit noise filtering. (1) Dual intra/inter embeddings and hybrid weighting [0.25,0.40,0.35] aim to surface the most on-point cases across question/support/entity fields; (2) AnglE contrastive embeddings mitigate cosine-similarity saturation to better discriminate relevance; (3) dataset validation (manual review, removing 40 offensive/hallucinated cases) cleans the casebase. There is no per-retrieval relevance evaluator, self-reflection, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware training.
memory_type: none (in the experiential/learning sense). The casebase is a static non-parametric case memory used for retrieval only; it is not an episodic/skill/workflow memory that grows or is updated. Best characterised as a static CBR case store.
write_back: False -- the system does not store new experiences/cases/answers back into the casebase during inference. The Retain phase of the CBR cycle is explicitly out of scope (retrieve-only integration).
online_growth: No -- the casebase is frozen after offline construction (2,084 cases) and does not grow at deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: Never -- no write-back mechanism is implemented (Retain phase not realised).
failure_experience_usage: None / success-only context: only the curated (synthetic, validated) positive QA cases form the retrievable store. No failed/negative trajectories are stored or retrieved. (AnglE's contrastive pre-training used positive/negative pairs, but that is encoder pre-training, not failure-experience memory in this system.)
memory_evolution_update: None -- the casebase is static/append-nothing at runtime; stored cases are never mutated, merged, delta-updated, refined, or pruned during deployment (the only pruning, removing 40 offensive cases, occurs once during offline casebase construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No -- retrieval is a fixed similarity top-k (kNN cosine over fixed embeddings) with hand-set hybrid weights. Case selection is not an RL/learned policy; the encoders are off-the-shelf (not even fine-tuned for this task).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No -- single-system private casebase; no multi-agent or cross-framework experience sharing. (The casebase author GPT-4 and the answer generator Mistral-7B are different models, but this is a generator/expert separation, not shared memory across agents.)
benchmarks: Australian Open Legal QA (ALQA) dataset (umarbutler/open-australian-legal-qa on HuggingFace), synthesised by GPT-4 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus; 2,124 question-support-answer triplets -> 2,084-case casebase after removing 40 offensive cases. A bespoke 32-case test set was created by pairing casebase cases sharing common legal acts and generating new questions with Mistral-7B (released as Ramitha/open-australian-legal-qa-test). Underlying corpus: Open Australian Legal Corpus (785 unique legal acts; e.g. Federal Court Rules, Civil Aviation Regulations 1998, Corporations Act 2001).
benchmark_family: QA -- domain-specific (legal) open-ended generative question answering with evidence grounding. Not in the standard multi-hop/web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL families; it is a single-domain legal QA evaluation on a self-constructed casebase + test set.
baselines: No-RAG (LLM with no case retrieval; Mistral-7B answering from parametric memory only) is the primary baseline comparator. Within CBR-RAG, ablative comparisons across encoders (BERT vs LegalBERT vs AnglEBERT), weighting schemes (question-only [1,0,0], support-only [0,1,0], entities-only [0,0,1], hybrid [0.25,0.40,0.35]), context type (support-only vs full-case), and k (k=1 vs k=3). No external system baselines beyond No-RAG.
key_metrics: (1) Retrieval: F1-score for retrieval@k (relevant set = the parent pair of cases each test case was derived from), swept over prime k in 1-37. (2) Generation: cosine similarity between the Mistral-embedding of the generated answer and the reference answer (semantic similarity to ground truth). Statistical significance via ANOVA + one-tailed paired T-tests.
headline_result: Hybrid AnglEBERT with weights [0.25,0.40,0.35] and k=3, injecting full cases, achieved the best generation quality at 0.9141 mean cosine similarity to the reference answer, vs 0.8967 for the No-RAG baseline -- a 1.94% average improvement. This setting significantly outperforms both No-RAG and Hybrid LegalBERT (k=3) at the 95% confidence level (and Hybrid BERT k=1 at 90%) by one-tailed T-test. For retrieval, Hybrid AnglEBERT [0.25,0.40,0.35] at k=3 was the best-performing retrieval configuration by F1@k.
ablations: (1) Encoder comparison: AnglEBERT > BERT and LegalBERT for both retrieval and generation; notably AnglEBERT (general contrastive embeddings) beats LegalBERT (domain-pre-trained, self-supervised), suggesting contrastive optimisation matters more than legal-domain pre-training when not fine-tuned to ALQA. LegalBERT embeddings were more densely clustered (higher baseline similarity), suggesting weaker discrimination. (2) Weighting/component ablation: question-only [1,0,0], support-only [0,1,0], entities-only [0,0,1] vs hybrid [0.25,0.40,0.35]; hybrid weighting gives the best retrieval F1. (3) Context type: full-case context (Q,S,E,A) generally outperforms support-text-only context in hybrid setups. (4) k ablation: k=3 outperforms k=1; all hybrid variants beat No-RAG. (5) Generation table (Table 4): No-RAG 0.8967; best Hybrid AnglEBERT k=3 full-case 0.9141.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- intrinsic retrieval quality (F1-score for retrieval@k, with a separately constructed parent-pair relevance ground truth, visualised as a heat-map over encoders/weights/k) is reported and analysed separately from the end-to-end generation quality (answer-to-reference cosine similarity). k=3 was selected from the retrieval analysis before the generation experiments.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome-oriented but with a decoupled retrieval-process metric: the final outcome is answer semantic similarity (cosine to reference); the intermediate retrieval process is scored by F1@k. There is no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise reasoning-quality metric; a qualitative domain-expert evaluation of answers is named as a future step.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified in cost/latency terms. The method adds one kNN retrieval over a small 2,084-case casebase plus prompt augmentation per query; no API-cost, latency, or token-count numbers are reported. The accuracy gain is modest (~1.94% mean cosine over No-RAG) and the No-RAG baseline is already high (0.8967) because Mistral's parametric memory covers many legal questions. Encoders are off-the-shelf (no fine-tuning cost).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: k=3 retrieved cases injected (k=1 as comparative baseline), selected from a retrieval sweep over prime k in 1-37. Context is either support-text-only or the full Q/S/E/A tuple per case. No explicit token budget or budget-capped truncation is reported; the paper notes that combining multiple neighbours into a coherent prompt is challenging (motivating future case-aggregation work).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Casebase: ALQA -> 2,084 cases (from 2,124 GPT-4-synthesised question-support-answer triplets, minus 40 offensive cases), each augmented with GPT-3.5-turbo-extracted entities; 785 unique legal acts, 57% of cases reference no legal act. Test set: 32 questions (from 35 generated, pruned to 32), constructed by selecting casebase case pairs sharing common legal acts and using Mistral-7B to synthesise new questions answerable only by combining both parent cases (so test questions are reasonably disjoint from any single casebase case); manually reviewed; released as Ramitha/open-australian-legal-qa-test. Answers are open-ended free text (verified by cosine similarity to a reference answer, not exact-match). Best-system signal: best generation cosine 0.9141 vs No-RAG 0.8967, indicating a relatively narrow improvement margin / difficult-to-beat parametric baseline.
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020); CBR knowledge-container theory and the CBR cycle (Aamodt & Plaza / Richter; HYPO -- Ashley 1991; CATO -- Aleven & Ashley 1997; textual CBR -- Bruninghaus & Ashley 2001, Wiratunga et al. 2004); hybrid CBR-IR legal information retrieval (Rissland & Daniels 1995); ensemble CBR-neural for content planning (Upadhyay & Massie 2022); BERT (Devlin et al. 2018); LegalBERT (Chalkidis et al. 2020); AnglE angle-optimized embeddings (Li & Li 2023) and Siamese networks (Bromley et al. 1993); Mistral-7B (Jiang et al. 2023); ALQA / Open Australian Legal Corpus (Butler 2024).
contrasts_with: No-RAG (LLM relying solely on parametric memory, prone to hallucination and lacking provenance). Standard RAG whose retrieval does not exploit CBR's varying matching strategies across content segments (the paper's central critique -- conventional RAG retrieval ignores CBR indexing-vocabulary / similarity-knowledge-container structure). Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2023) and other sophisticated fact-identifying RAG mechanisms are cited as related retrieval approaches. Domain-pre-trained LegalBERT is contrasted against contrastive AnglEBERT (contrastive optimisation found more important than domain pre-training when not fine-tuned).
lineage: Group D (case-based planning / case-based reasoning lineage). A concrete CBR-RAG reference: operationalises the CBR Retrieve stage (indexing vocabulary + similarity knowledge containers; intra/inter/hybrid dual embeddings) inside an LLM RAG pipeline for legal QA. Sits in the CBR-for-RAG sub-lineage alongside CBR-KBQA (retrieve-reuse-revise for semantic parsing) but is retrieve-only, explicitly ICCBR-grounded, and a touchstone for later case-based agentic-RAG work; followed by the authors' own ensemble-LLM CBR legal follow-up (Abeyratne, ICCBR 2025).
